name: boat.dev

modes.label: On-demand (flat per size, per second while running)
modes.commit_note: No commit/reserved/always-on discount exists; a 24/7 default sandbox is simply 730 h x $0.036 = $26.28/month.
modes.note: Flat price per size, independent of CPU/RAM use (idle-but-running bills full rate). Billing starts when the machine is provisioned, before the sandbox is ready (docs.boat.dev/concepts). Stopped = no compute charge; the disk is kept free for at least 14 days, then can be deleted unless saved as a saved snapshot. xlarge needs the $100+ plan (no contact needed) and costs 5.56x default for 4x resources (+39% per vCPU). Disk is fixed per size (51/51/111/251 GB of user data); more disk means a bigger size. Every sandbox runs as a full VM on bare-metal hosts dedicated to boat: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X and Ryzen 9 9950X (docs.boat.dev/machines/virtualization); vCPUs are shared, not dedicated cores. The perf number was measured on a 9950X host.

storage.note: Stopped disk kept free for at least 14 days, then eligible for deletion (resume fails with 409 snapshot_data_expired). Saved snapshots: 10 per $20 of plan per seat included, then $0.056 per snapshot per day, no scheduled expiry; charged per snapshot, not per GiB (not modelled).

network.note: Public IPv6 on every sandbox plus outbound IPv4. Some sandboxes have no IPv4 of their own: SSH (shared IPv4 host:port) and HTTPS public URLs still work over IPv4, raw ports are IPv6-only there. No dedicated or static IPv4 is sold. The IP changes at each resume. boat does not bill egress (docs.boat.dev/pricing, Included at no cost).

plans.name: Trial
plans.note: 7-day free trial, card required at Stripe Checkout. One trial per person; organizations get no trial; repeat sign-ups can be refused. 25 h of VM time in total, 2 at once, small/default only, auto-stop required (2 h max), 5 starts/min, 25/h, 75/day, no new saved snapshots. Unless cancelled, Stripe charges the chosen plan after 7 days.

plans.name: $20/mo
plans.note: Fee = $20 of VM time for that month; unused time expires at period end. Overage from the wallet at the same rates (wallet money never expires). Included starts 12/min, 60/h, 200/day; create, fork and resume each count (a resume onto the kept machine does not). Extra starts $0.03-$0.07 each from the wallet, up to 6x the included hour/day limits (3x per minute, max 1,200/day), then 429; boat never queues a start. Extra starts on the invoice are off by default, capped at $80 per seat per month. The estimator models the included limits only. Session unlimited with auto-stop off (numeric TTL max 30 d); default TTL 1 h from creation or resume.
plans.seat_note: Organization plans cost the plan price per seat; each seat adds the included time. On $20/$100/$500 each extra seat adds 20% of the concurrency and start limits, never above the next plan's limits; on $2,000 each seat adds the full limits (docs.boat.dev/organizations/seats-and-limits, 2026-11-08). The estimator still scales limits 1:1 per seat.

Extra starts $0.03-$0.07 each from the wallet, up to 6x the included hour/day limits (3x per minute, max 5,040/day), then 429; boat never queues a start. Extra starts on the invoice are off by default, capped at $400 per seat per month. The estimator models the included limits only.

free.conditions: card required (Stripe Checkout); one trial per person, none for organizations; 25 h of VM time; charges the chosen plan after 7 days unless cancelled

features.ip_note: Default datacenter IPs; a custom Chromium fork keeps X, LinkedIn and most sites working (owner-reported)

perf_source: Every boat sandbox in this run ran on an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X host. boat also places some sandboxes on other host classes that the run did not measure (a Hetzner-host sandbox did 8.88 runs/s in the boat team's 2026-08-24 run: https://github.com/AnicetNgrt/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/blob/provider/ascii-box/docs/results/2026-08-24-cpu/leaderboard.md). CPU 28.06 runs/s: V8 Web Tooling Benchmark (Phoronix node-web-tooling), StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks run 37073680030 (2026-10-03), row "boat", median of 5 sandboxes at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target, rank 2 of 15 (shared: the run cannot separate it from the providers at the same rank). https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/blob/297198a96ee827df5edcd918bd37b949526cfe20/LEADERBOARD.md

knobs.label: Idle time billed until TTL auto-stop (× session hours)
knobs.why: boat.dev has no idle auto-stop: a running sandbox bills the full size rate, busy or idle, until `boat stop` or its TTL expires. TTL counts from creation/resume (default 1 h; forks reset to 1 h), so a 20-min task left to the default TTL bills 3x. Default 1 = stopped when work ends; with --no-auto-stop the tail is unbounded (use always-on instead).

caveats: Battleships is made by boat.dev; boat.dev's numbers come from its public docs and are held to the same standard as every other provider.
boat is not in the ComputeSDK benchmarks: cold_start_ms, burst_tti_ms, dax_s unknown.

The CPU benchmark ran on a 9950X host. The fleet also has Ryzen 7 9700X hosts (docs.boat.dev/machines/virtualization); the user cannot pick the host, and disk flush (fsync) latency differs by host class.
Plan fee is 100% VM time for that month and expires at period end (effective $20/month minimum). Overage is paid from a wallet at the same rates; wallet money never expires (docs.boat.dev/faq).
Trial is one-time 25 h of VM time (about $0.90 of default time), 2 at once, small/default, TTL <= 2 h, 75 starts/day, card required; it cannot be extended with paid usage.

No idle auto-stop: TTL counts from creation/resume (default 1 h; forks get 1 h unless set); a running agent prompt moves the deadline. Idle-but-running bills full size rate. Auto-stop can be off on paid plans, numeric TTL max 30 days (docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks/auto-stop).

Start limits per plan (create, fork and resume each count; a resume onto the kept machine does not): $20 12/60/200 per min/hour/day, $100 30/210/840, $500 65/420/1,680, $2,000 90/600/2,400. Extra starts cost $0.03-$0.07 each up to 6x the hour/day limit (3x per minute), then fail with 429; boat never queues a start (docs.boat.dev/limits). The estimator enforces the included per-minute and per-day limits and does not add extra-start fees.

Organization seats: plan price per seat; each seat adds the included time; extra seats add 20% of the limits below the $2,000 plan, the full limits on $2,000 (docs.boat.dev/organizations/seats-and-limits). The estimator scales limits 1:1 with seats, which overstates boat's limits for teams below $2,000.
Egress is not billed (docs.boat.dev/pricing, Included at no cost); no published cap.

Network: public IPv6 on every sandbox and outbound IPv4. Some sandboxes have no IPv4 of their own (SSH through a shared IPv4 host:port, HTTPS URLs over IPv4, raw ports IPv6-only). No dedicated IPv4 is sold, and the IP changes at each resume (docs.boat.dev/faq).

Stopped disk: kept free for at least 14 days after the stop, then eligible for deletion (cleanup is report-only in production today); resume then fails with 409 snapshot_data_expired. Saved snapshots have no scheduled expiry: 10 per $20 of plan per seat included, then $0.056 per snapshot per day (docs.boat.dev/pricing). Per-snapshot charge, not per GiB, so snapshot_gib_month=0 holds and the fee is not modelled.
Saved snapshots above the included count and the AI credentials proxy still charge while sandboxes are stopped (docs.boat.dev/pricing).

Snapshots: every minute while running plus one at each stop. Filesystem only: memory, running programs, /tmp, ~/.cache (except Playwright/Deno), journal logs, Docker build cache and untagged images are not saved; resume = reboot. A machine failure loses writes after the last good snapshot (docs.boat.dev/cli-reference); with snapshots off there is no backup.
No extra-disk purchase: disk is fixed per size (51/51/111/251 GB of user data), so disk needs can force upsizing. included_disk_gib=51 refers to the default size.
vCPUs are shared, not dedicated physical cores (docs.boat.dev/machines/virtualization).
Machines in Germany, Finland and France; no region choice and no US/Asia option. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU (docs.boat.dev/compliance), so eu_data_residency=false.
Custom environments via saved snapshots and setup scripts, not Dockerfile/OCI images (custom_image=false).
Empty wallet: 24 h grace, then snapshot and stop; earlier if new debt passes 25% of the plan price ($50 minimum) (docs.boat.dev/billing).
Billing starts when the machine is provisioned, before the sandbox is ready (docs.boat.dev/concepts state table).

The AI credentials proxy is optional and paid: $1 for each UTC day it is on plus $1 per 1,000 proxied requests (docs.boat.dev/ai-credentials#pricing). Bedrock and the Kimi Code sign-in are not proxied. The estimator does not add this charge.
Higher limits than the $2,000 plan only on a custom plan; per-member usage and concurrency caps are available to org owners.
SOC 2 in progress (no report). 99.95% measured sandbox uptime; no SLA published (docs.boat.dev/compliance).

fleet.verification: Trial eligibility restrictions; paid plan and payment method required for paid limits and disabling auto-stop. No universal ID/KYC requirement stated; terms reserve additional verification.
fleet.tiers: Trial 2; $20/month 100; $100/month 300; $500/month 1,000; $2,000/month 2,000. Plan payments become VM time for that month. Extra org seats add 20% of the limits below $2,000 and the full limits on $2,000; above that, a custom plan.
fleet.notes: boat.dev: plan upgrades apply at once. Starts (create, fork, resume) are capped per plan: $20 12/min, 60/hour, 200/day included, up to 1,200/day with paid extra starts ($0.03-$0.07 each); $100 30/210/840; $500 65/420/1,680; $2,000 90/600/2,400. A refused start fails with 429 and is not queued. A 1,000-sandbox limit is not a 1,000-start burst. Trial 25 h, 2-hour TTL max. xlarge self-serve on $100+.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: They are taken **every minute** while the sandbox is ready or idle, and a final one when it **stops**.
snapshot_auto.note: Automatic incremental filesystem snapshots every minute while running plus a final one on stop (manual stop, TTL auto-stop, balance cutoff); resume restores the latest. Disk only: 'Running processes, memory, open ports' are not captured, so resume = reboot (enabled systemd services restart). A stop is refused if the final snapshot fails. Can be turned off per account/sandbox ('snapshots off').

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Freeze a sandbox's current state under a name (`boat snapshot <id> <name>` in the CLI). Answers `202` immediately with the snapshot in `saving`; a running sandbox takes a fresh capture first, which can run minutes.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Named (saved) snapshots of running or stopped sandboxes. Each plan includes 10 per $20 of plan per seat; each extra one costs $0.056 a day ($1.68 for 30 days) (docs.boat.dev/pricing). No scheduled expiry, shareable with another account by a share code; `boat new --from <name>` boots any number of new sandboxes from them; `boat fork` copies a sandbox's current filesystem into a new one. Filesystem only, no memory. The snapshots page also says 'You never take one by hand' about the rolling per-minute snapshots.

harness_api.quote: Queue a natural-language work item for an agent harness (Codex, Claude Code, pi, OpenCode, or Prime Agent) inside the sandbox. Observe progress with `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events`.
harness_api.note: POST /prompt + events stream, GET /conversations (list/resume), POST /steer (mid-turn follow-up), interrupt (all or one conversation), per-prompt harness/model switch with context carry-over; CLI `boat prompt`/`boat steer`/`boat conversations`; Python/TS SDKs. integrated-agents.md also lists Kimi Code: 'Claude Code, Codex, pi, OpenCode, Prime Agent, and Kimi Code'.

egress_allowlist.quote: Boat does not yet enforce Eve's fine-grained network policies. The backend accepts `"allow-all"` and throws `EveSandboxUnsupportedError` for stricter policies (`"deny-all"`, allow-lists, subnet rules), so you never get a false sense of isolation.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side egress policy anywhere in the docs; FAQ points to in-VM controls instead. Stated on the Eve integration page, not a platform-level 'not supported' statement, hence medium.

egress_http_rules.quote: Boat does not yet enforce Eve's fine-grained network policies.
egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side egress control of any kind, so no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: A fresh `host <port>` URL is protected by default and includes `_token`.
ingress_rules.note: HTTPS URLs only for ports you expose with `host <port>` (up to 50), token-gated by default or public. No IP allowlists/security groups. Raw access to the sandbox IP is opened by the user 'with `ufw`' inside the VM, i.e. a guest firewall, not a provider-side control.

guest_firewall.quote: Sandboxes are full VMs with sudo, so you can add any controls you need inside them (firewall rules, proxies, encryption).
guest_firewall.note: Full VM with its own kernel and sudo; hosting.md also tells users to open raw ports 'yourself with `ufw`'.

secret_proxy.quote: Without the proxy, a sandbox holds your real keys and sign-ins. Anyone with a shell in it can copy them. With the proxy on, the real keys never enter the sandbox.
secret_proxy.note: AI credentials proxy, off by default and paid ($1 per UTC day it is on, plus $1 per 1,000 proxied requests). Covers Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter/LLM Gateway/DeepSeek/Moonshot/Mistral keys, Claude/ChatGPT/Mistral Vibe sign-ins, and custom APIs: 'A custom API is a secret for any HTTPS API, such as Stripe or your own service', reached through `$<NAME>_BASE_URL`. Not proxied: AWS Bedrock and the Kimi Code sign-in (withheld while the proxy is on). Environment variables, the GitHub token and other secrets still enter the sandbox.

credential_injection.quote: Your sandboxes get the AI credentials of a **credential profile**: Claude and ChatGPT sign-ins, API keys, and custom APIs.
credential_injection.note: Credential profiles (per account or organization, chosen per environment) inject model keys, sign-ins and custom-API secrets as environment variables; a credential can hold several accounts and be switched to another account for every sandbox at once, running ones included. Environment variables and the GitHub token are injected too (environments.md).

volume_attach.quote: "Disk" is what your own files can grow to; the operating system and pre-installed tools sit outside it.
volume_attach.note: Disk is fixed per size (51/51/111/251 GB of user data); no volume product, attach API or extra-disk purchase. More disk = bigger size.

volume_shared.quote: "Disk" is what your own files can grow to; the operating system and pre-installed tools sit outside it.
volume_shared.note: No volumes or shared filesystem at all; sharing only by copy (fork, named snapshot, snapshot download).

captcha_solving.quote: Every sandbox is a Linux VM with a curated set of tools available from the moment you SSH in.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Boat.dev is a general-purpose Linux sandbox/VM with SSH, desktop and browser access; nothing in its docs, API reference, or integrations pages mentions CAPTCHA solving as a feature.

fork_running.quote: They are taken every minute while the sandbox is ready or idle, and a final one when it stops.
fork_running.note: Fork requires only a completed snapshot, not a stopped sandbox: 'boat fork <id> ... Requires the source sandbox to have a completed snapshot. Forking copies the snapshotted filesystem into a new Sandbox ... The source sandbox is never modified' (https://docs.boat.dev/llms-full.txt, fork-sandbox / CLI reference). Since running sandboxes are auto-snapshotted every minute, a running sandbox always has a recent completed snapshot to fork from, and the source keeps running unaffected.

wake_on_request.quote: Sandboxes have an auto-stop timer. ... Resuming a stopped sandbox restarts the timer.
wake_on_request.note: No mechanism documented for a stopped/archived sandbox to wake automatically when an inbound request (e.g. a hosted HTTPS URL) arrives; every doc path to bring a stopped sandbox back is an explicit `boat resume` / POST /sandboxes/{id}/resume call. Hosting docs describe the proxy routing to a running sandbox but never mention auto-resuming an archived one on request.

own_agent_api.quote: Queue a natural-language work item for an agent harness (Codex, Claude Code, pi, OpenCode, or Prime Agent) inside the sandbox.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Boat's `/prompt` (harness_api) drives third-party CODING harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, pi, OpenCode, Prime Intellect's Prime Agent, Kimi Code) inside the VM. There is no first-party Boat-branded browser/computer-use/research task agent product distinct from these installed coding harnesses.

static_egress_ip.quote: The IP address changes at every resume and fork.
static_egress_ip.note: The outbound IP is that of the current machine and changes at every resume and fork; no static egress IP is sold.

max_session_h.quote: For work that should keep running until you stop it yourself, disable auto-stop when you create the sandbox or update an existing sandbox's TTL to `null`: boat new --no-auto-stop
max_session_h.note: Default auto-stop TTL is 1 hour from creation/resume; a numeric TTL caps at 30 days, but auto-stop off (paid plans only; the trial requires a TTL of 2 h or less) removes the timer, so the sandbox runs until stopped.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Resume behaves like a server reboot: systemd services you enabled start again automatically. Processes you ran by hand (dev servers, background jobs, tunnels, desktop sessions) do not survive; restart them, or make them a systemd service.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Same reboot semantics apply to fork (fork copies the filesystem snapshot, not running memory); snapshots/forks are filesystem-only, so no running process/memory state carries over.

custom_image.quote: Boat runs a ready image; it doesn't build Docker images. ... The Dockerfile is read only for its final-stage WORKDIR; build steps (RUN / COPY / …) are not executed
custom_image.note: Sandboxes start from Boat's own Ubuntu 24.04 base or from named snapshots (`boat snapshot save` / `boat new --from <name>`), never from a user-supplied image; install steps must run as commands after boot.

image_oci.quote: Boat runs a ready image; it doesn't build Docker images. Some Harbor features don't map to Boat today and raise a clear error: network policies (no-network / allow-lists), Docker image builds / Compose, and GPUs / TPUs / Windows.
image_oci.note: No way to start a machine from your own Docker/OCI image; Docker runs *inside* the sandbox (docker_inside=true) but the sandbox itself is always Boat's fixed Ubuntu 24.04 base.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Boat has no idle timer. The auto-stop TTL counts from creation or resume, never from last activity, so run your own countdown and call `boat stop` a few seconds to a couple of minutes after the agent finishes.
auto_stop_idle.note: Auto-stop is a fixed TTL from creation/resume/fork (default 1h, max 30d, or disabled with --no-auto-stop), not idle-detection; a busy sandbox is stopped exactly the same as an idle one at TTL expiry.

volumes.quote: "Disk" is what your own files can grow to; the operating system and pre-installed tools sit outside it.
volumes.note: Disk is a fixed per-size preset (51/51/111/251 GB of user data for small/default/large/xlarge); no separate volume product, attach API, or extra-disk purchase exists in the docs or API reference.

mcp_server.quote: The tools come from the Cua Driver, preinstalled on every sandbox and registered as an MCP server named `computer` for all six harnesses
mcp_server.note: The only MCP server involved is `computer` (Cua Driver desktop-control tools) *inside* the sandbox for coding harnesses to use; Boat does not ship an MCP server that lets an external client control Boat's own sandbox-management API (create/list/stop/etc.) – that surface is CLI/REST/SDK only.

gpu.quote: GPU | None. Graphics run on the CPU (the desktop and headless Chrome work)
gpu.note: Confirmed again in the Harbor integration page: "Some Harbor features don't map to Boat today ... GPUs / TPUs / Windows."

windows.quote: Some Harbor features don't map to Boat today and raise a clear error: network policies (no-network / allow-lists), Docker image builds / Compose, and GPUs / TPUs / Windows.
windows.note: Also machines.md: every sandbox is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Linux 6.8, x86_64 – Linux-only, no Windows machine option.

macos.note: Product is a Linux VM sandbox platform; no macOS machine type is offered or mentioned anywhere in the docs. macOS is plainly outside what this product is.

arm64.note: Only x86_64 machines are documented (AMD Ryzen 7 9700X and Ryzen 9 9950X hosts); no ARM/aarch64 option anywhere in docs or API.

self_host.quote: Your plan, environment, sandboxes and settings live on your account, not on the machine.
self_host.note: Boat is a hosted multi-tenant SaaS (account/plan/dashboard/billing model); no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option, binary, or Helm chart is documented anywhere.

byoc.quote: Sandboxes run on machines in Germany, Finland and France. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU.
byoc.note: boat runs every sandbox on its own machines; no region choice and no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment in pricing, FAQ or API docs. Quote replaced 2026-11-08: the old one ("Your data and snapshots stay there") is out of date.

open_source.quote: boat is the user's own product.
open_source.note: No OSI-licensed core-product repository is published; the only open-source component mentioned is the third-party Cua Driver dependency (github.com/trycua/cua) used for computer-use tooling, not the Boat sandbox platform itself.

soc2.quote: Do you have compliance certifications? Not yet. SOC 2 is in progress. Sandboxes are full VMs with sudo, so you can add any controls you need inside them (firewall rules, proxies, encryption).
soc2.note: SOC 2 explicitly not yet attested (in progress).

hipaa.quote: Do you have compliance certifications? Not yet. SOC 2 is in progress.
hipaa.note: No HIPAA eligibility or BAA is mentioned anywhere in the docs; the compliance FAQ names only SOC 2 (in progress) and nothing else.

sso.quote: GitHub, Google and an emailed 6-digit code are three ways in, on both the CLI and the dashboard.
sso.note: Only GitHub/Google OAuth and email-code login are documented; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO option is mentioned anywhere in the docs.

private_network.quote: Boat does not yet enforce Eve's fine-grained network policies. The backend accepts "allow-all" and throws EveSandboxUnsupportedError for stricter policies ("deny-all", allow-lists, subnet rules)
private_network.note: No VPC/private-networking product exists; also confirmed by the Harbor integration note that "network policies (no-network / allow-lists)" are unsupported. Sandboxes get a public IPv6 address and outbound IPv4; some have no IPv4 address of their own.

live_resize.quote: Can I resize a sandbox? Yes. Pass `--type` to `resume` or `fork` to move a sandbox between `small`, `default`, and `large`.
live_resize.note: Resizing only happens via `resume` (a stop/restart cycle) or `fork` (a new machine); a running sandbox's CPU/RAM cannot be changed in place without recreating/restarting it, so live_resize is correctly false.

public_ipv4.quote: Every sandbox has a public IPv6 address and outbound IPv4. Some sandboxes have no IPv4 address of their own. SSH and public URLs work over IPv4 anyway. The IP address changes at each resume, so use a public URL.
public_ipv4.note: No dedicated IPv4: every sandbox has a public IPv6 and outbound IPv4. Some sandboxes have no IPv4 of their own; SSH then goes through a shared IPv4 host:port (sshEndpoint) and HTTPS URLs work over IPv4. Bare-metal guests are IPv6-only (backend machineProvider.service.ts).

usage_api.quote: Machine time one sandbox consumed, and what it costs, so you can bill your own users per sandbox. Same meter as `GET /limits`: billable seconds with the sandbox type's multiplier applied, paused past a refused stop, never counting time stopped.

eu_data_residency.quote: Sandboxes run on machines in Germany, Finland and France. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU.
eu_data_residency.note: Partial: compute is in the EU, but snapshot copies (the user disk) can be stored outside the EU, so it does not meet an EU data residency requirement.

persist_scope.quote: A snapshot saves the parts of the disk that you changed. It does not save the operating system that every machine already has.
persist_scope.note: boat snapshots the disk every minute while the sandbox runs and once more at each stop; resume restores it. Saved: home folders, folders you create at /, your changes in /etc, /usr, /opt, /root, /srv and /var (installed packages), Docker named volumes, containers and tagged images. Not saved: /tmp, journal logs, ~/.cache (except Playwright and Deno), the Docker build cache, untagged images, memory and running programs; a resume is like a reboot. A stopped disk is kept for at least 14 days, then can be deleted unless saved as a saved snapshot. A machine failure loses writes after the last good snapshot; with snapshots off there is no backup.

desktop.quote: The full desktop over Moonlight (WebRTC), 1920x1080 at 60 fps
desktop.note: Built in on every sandbox. No GPU: graphics run on the CPU.

browser.note: Chrome is preinstalled and can be streamed on its own with `boat browser <id>`.

raw_tcp_inbound.quote: Some sandboxes have no public IPv4 address. Then `boat info` shows `sshEndpoint`, and `ip` is an IPv6 address. Only clients with IPv6 can reach a raw port there.
raw_tcp_inbound.note: Raw inbound TCP/UDP to the sandbox IP works; on sandboxes without their own IPv4 it is IPv6-only.

locations_quote: Sandboxes run on machines in Germany, Finland and France. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU.
